title: What to watch at tomorrow's open
text: Stocks rose on Monday. The S&P 500 fund SPY closed at $765.28, up 0.7%, and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ closed at $712.18, up 1.1%. Chip and tech names led the way, while Alphabet and Meta slipped. Tomorrow, watch how stocks start after this gain. Alphabet and Microsoft are expected to report results on Wednesday, October 28, and Amazon on Thursday, October 29. Big news can move prices fast. This is for learning, not advice.

title: Lockheed Martin jumps 5.1%
text: Lockheed Martin closed at $635.20, up 5.1%, a big move for a stock with a beta of only 0.10. Beta tells us how much a stock usually moves compared with the whole market, and a low beta means it normally moves less. We could not confirm what caused today's jump. Last week the company reported a record backlog (orders not yet finished) of $292.0 billion. The price is now just 0.5% below the average analyst target of $638.22. A target is only an opinion, not a promise.

title: Chip stocks climb together
text: AMD rose 2.8% to $531.28, NVIDIA rose 2.4% to $216.02, Broadcom rose 2.3% and Vertiv rose 2.8%. The Nasdaq technology group gained about 1.0% on average. Even so, Vertiv is still 47.4% below its 52 week high, and AMD has a risk score of 7.4 out of 10 because its price swings are big. One good day does not tell us what comes next.

title: Alphabet and Meta slip before earnings
text: Meta fell 1.9% to $630.56 and Alphabet fell 1.1% to $316.80. Communication services, the sector group that includes both, lost about 1.2% on Nasdaq. Alphabet reports on Wednesday, so traders may be nervous about the numbers. Prices often move before and after a report, in either direction.

title: Lesson 23: What is a stock split?
text: A stock split is when a company cuts each share into smaller pieces. In a 2 for 1 split, if you own 1 share worth $100, you end up with 2 shares worth $50 each. Your total stays $100. It is like cutting a pizza into more slices: the pizza is the same size. Companies sometimes split so each share costs less and feels easier to buy. A split does not make a company worth more by itself. What matters is how well the business is doing. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell anything.

title: What this board covers
